verdict.justification: Both proposals correctly calculate the INR 103,910 per-pack saving and cover the requested equity structure, Delhi operations, sourcing flow, volumes, and localisation phases. A is stronger on financial accuracy: it correctly identifies imported content as “97.2% of the new cost,” whereas B twice describes roughly 85% of cost as remaining imported or USD-linked, confusing the original cost base with the localised cost base. This materially understates the continuing import dependence, a key risk for the CPO. A also provides quantified downside scenarios, capex-recovery sensitivity, and more actionable approval gates with named owners and an imported-pack fallback during qualification. Both appropriately distinguish gross savings from a final investment case and flag the need to validate regulatory eligibility. B is more concise and executive-friendly, and A would benefit from trimming its working-file commentary, but A's more accurate risk presentation and stronger decision framework make it the preferable deliverable.

decisive_issues.issue: Uses the original pack-cost denominator to describe residual import and forex exposure; imported components actually represent approximately 97.2% of the localised pack cost.
decisive_issues.quote: Residual exposure: ~85% of pack cost stays USD-linked, so the forex benefit is partial (see Section 5).

decisive_issues.issue: Repeats the understated imported-cost share in the main risk assessment, weakening the CPO's view of continuing import dependence.
decisive_issues.quote: ~85% of cost stays imported; tariff, forex and geopolitical/shipping risk persist; cells are the highest-value item
